note: Knowledge for the SPC chatbot (simple version, goes with spc_chatbot_implementation.md v4.0). Causes and checks are possibilities to verify on the floor, not facts. Review with JK Process and Quality before go-live. Tolerances must match the KPI job.

limits.spec: The parameter's tolerance below (setpoint +/- tolerance, a fixed range, or from the data), the same as the KPI job. Used for 'why is Cp/Cpk low' and 'crossing the spec'.
limits.control: centre +/- 1.12 x (UCL - LCL), with centre = (UCL + LCL) / 2. The chart limits are for averages of 5 pieces, and single pieces vary more. Used for 'crossing the control limit'.

patterns.normal: No reading is outside the limits. No page: say the data looks normal.
patterns.spikes: 5 or fewer readings outside, or 1% of pieces or fewer.
patterns.off_target: More than that, with 80% or more of them on the same side.
patterns.jumping: More than that, on both sides.
patterns.no_reading: Checked separately: the value is blank, or 0 or below (for splices and conicity only blank counts).

no_reading.has_happened: The width gauge sent 0 or nothing for some pieces.
can_happen_because: Line stopped, or no tread under the gauge
Gauge blinded by water, steam or dirt, or the tread edge not found
Gauge signal or communication lost

what_to_do.check: Check the gauge signal and tag quality; clean the lens or window
Check whether the line was stopped or changing over at that time

off_target.has_happened: Tread is consistently wider (or narrower) than the setpoint.
can_happen_because: Takeaway speed against extrusion speed wrong: faster stretches the tread narrower, slower leaves it wider
Extruder output (weight per metre) off; width follows output
Compound swells more or less than normal (Mooney, mixing temperature, filler dispersion)
Wrong, worn or badly seated die or insert after a change
Width gauge zero, span or edge setting wrong; a hotter tread also reads wider

what_to_do.check: Compare conveyor speed ratios with the recipe
Check whether weight on the same pieces is off the same way: both off means a real output change, width alone points to the gauge
Check Mooney and mixer dump temperature of the batches in use
Check the die ID against the recipe and gauge the die opening
Measure 5 pieces by hand and compare with the gauge; check the gauge with a reference bar

spikes.has_happened: A few pieces are much wider or narrower than the rest.
can_happen_because: Lumps, scorched particles, hard spots or foreign matter in the compound
Feed strip break or feed hiccup on one extruder
Gauge misreading: tread curl, water drops, steam or the tread wandering
First pieces after a stop or a speed change

what_to_do.check: Inspect the flagged pieces; check the head and preformer for scorched rubber
Check that extruder's head pressure and motor load at those times
If the same pieces have normal weight, check the gauge

jumping.has_happened: Width swings above and below the limits.
can_happen_because: Line still settling after a stop or start-up
Extruder output pulsing (feed disturbances, screw fill, surge)
Screw or line speed not steady
Rework or mixed compound batches
Takeaway or dancer speed control hunting

what_to_do.check: If it happened right after a stop, review the start-up procedure
Look at a fast head-pressure trend; check the feed roll and feed strip
Check drive speed logs and control loop tuning
Check rework dosing records

no_reading.has_happened: The scale sent 0 or a negative value for some pieces.
can_happen_because: Line stopped, or nothing on the scale
Scale tared while loaded, so it reads negative when empty
Load cell or signal fault

what_to_do.check: Zero the scale with an empty belt and check it with test weights
Check whether the line was stopped at that time

off_target.has_happened: Tread is consistently heavier (or lighter) than the setpoint.
can_happen_because: Takeaway speed or weight-control target wrong, so the tread is stretched too much or too little
One of the five extruders under- or over-feeding (total weight can look right while one layer is wrong)
Compound Mooney off, so output at the set screw speed is off
Density off: trapped air or wrong compound
Scale zero or span wrong, water or rubber build-up on the scale, or the belt rubbing the frame

what_to_do.check: Compare the weight-control target and conveyor speeds with the recipe
Compare each extruder's head pressure, temperature and screw speed with the recipe
Check batch Mooney and run a specific-gravity test
Re-weigh 5 pieces on a certified bench scale

spikes.has_happened: A few pieces are much heavier or lighter than the rest.
can_happen_because: Feed strip break on one extruder
Lumps, scorch or hard spots in the compound
First pieces after a restart
Double or partial piece, or pieces overlapping on the scale

what_to_do.check: Check each extruder's head pressure at those times
Check the cut length of the same pieces
Inspect the scale area for knocks or contact

jumping.has_happened: Weight swings above and below the limits.
can_happen_because: Line still settling after a stop or start-up
Extruder output pulsing (feed, screw fill, surge)
Weight control loop reacting too hard for the scale's delay
Rework or mixed compound batches
Scale vibration or belt tracking

what_to_do.check: If it happened right after a stop, review the start-up procedure
Check a fast head-pressure trend and the feed strips
Review the weight loop tuning
Check rework dosing records

no_reading.has_happened: The cut-length reading was 0 or blank for some pieces.
can_happen_because: Line stopped, or the skiver not cutting
Length sensor or encoder signal lost
Communication lost, or the tag not updating

what_to_do.check: Check the skiver alarm log and the encoder signal
Check whether the line was stopped at that time

off_target.has_happened: Tread pieces are cut consistently shorter (or longer) than the setpoint.
can_happen_because: Shrinkage allowance in the skiver setpoint wrong for this compound or tread temperature
Tread hotter or cooler at the skiver (cooling water temperature or flow, line speed)
Tread stretched over the conveyors by a speed difference, then pulling back after the cut
Measuring wheel worn, encoder scaling wrong, or the tread slipping on the belt
Length taken between different reference edges of the skived ends

what_to_do.check: Hand-measure 5 to 10 cut pieces at booking and compare with the logged length
Take an IR reading of tread temperature at the skiver; check cooling water temperatures
Check conveyor speed ratios against the recipe
Mark tread and belt with chalk over 10 m and recalibrate the encoder

spikes.has_happened: A few pieces are much longer or shorter than the rest.
can_happen_because: Missed, double or partial cut, or the skiver re-synchronising after a stop
Tread skewed at the cutter or measuring point
Edge misread because of water or scrap
Length value logged twice (it can update a few seconds after the cut counter)

what_to_do.check: Check the skiver alarm log at those times
Check tread guiding before the skiver
Ask Automation when the length value updates relative to the cut counter

jumping.has_happened: Cut length swings above and below the limits.
can_happen_because: Line still settling after a stop or start-up
Tread slipping by different amounts (wet or dirty belt, low belt tension)
Tension between conveyors or dancers varying, so stretch and shrinkage vary
Flying-cut synchronisation or servo tuning, or line speed not steady
Weight control loop changing the stretch

what_to_do.check: If it happened right after a stop, review the start-up procedure
Check belt condition, cleanliness and tension
Check dancer and conveyor speed trends
Check skiver servo tuning; scatter well beyond the skiver's own accuracy points upstream

can_happen_because: Edge not found by the camera: glare, a shadow at a lifted end, weak light or dirty optics
Machine in manual mode, the station bypassed, or the tyre aborted or rebuilt
A missing value stored as 0, or a wrong tag in the data path

what_to_do.check: Clean the optics, check the lighting and check the camera on its calibration target
Check whether the machine was in manual mode at that time
Compare the raw machine value with the value in the data lake

off_target.has_happened: The tread is applied consistently longer (or shorter) than the setpoint.
can_happen_because: Tread booked too early and still shrinking, or used at a different temperature

Cut pieces contracting while they wait for the drum (longer waits shrink more)
Setpoint not matching the drum, or wrong in the recipe

what_to_do.check: Measure 5 tread pieces by hand and compare with the logged length
Check the tread splice on the same tyres: too short gives an open splice, too long an overlap
Check the extrusion line data for the same tread lot (speed, booking temperature, rework)
Clean the measuring wheel; check wear, contact spring and encoder; jog a fixed length against a tape
Check festoon loop limits, dancer, brake and wind-up tension, and the peel point
Check the setpoint against the spec, the drum circumference and the recipe change log

no_reading.has_happened: RFV was 0 or blank for some tyres; a real force variation cannot be 0.
can_happen_because: Test aborted: the bead did not seal or the tyre did not inflate
Tyre skipped, or a load cell or data-acquisition fault
Barcode join failed, so the result did not attach to the tyre

what_to_do.check: Check the tester alarm and status log, and the test pressure of the same tyres
Retest those tyres

off_target.has_happened: Many tyres have RFV above the limit; the RFV level has shifted up.
can_happen_because: Building drum or transfer ring out of round or misaligned
Heavy spots from long splice overlaps, light spots from open splices, or splices stacked at the same angle
Tread gauge variation or belt cord disorder
Green tyres deformed in storage (sidewall crushed, bead out of round)
Mould or press effect: segment mismatch, off-centre loading, worn bladder, post-cure inflation missing or late
Tester: loadwheel out of round, rim runout, test pressure or load off

what_to_do.check: Split the tyres by building machine (green tyre barcode), press, cavity, mould and tester: following one building machine points to building, a press or mould to curing, one tester (check tyre too) to the tester
On the building machine it follows: check drum runout and transfer ring alignment
Audit splices and tread cut length; check splice stagger against the spec
On the press it follows: check loader centring and the bladder cure count
Run the master or check tyre on the tester

spikes.has_happened: A few tyres have much higher RFV than the rest.
can_happen_because: Tread splice gap (tread too short) or overlap (too long), or a cord overlap
Green tyre crushed in handling or storage
Mould segment bite or debris
Bead not seated properly, or a one-off pressure dip during the test

what_to_do.check: Remount and retest the tyre; if the value drops, it was the measurement
Inspect the tyre at the RFV peak for a splice problem
Check the tread length and splice of the same tyres on the building machine (barcode)

jumping.has_happened: RFV swings above and below the control limits.
can_happen_because: Tyres from different building machines, presses or sizes mixed in one chart
Measurement repeatability: bead seating, lubrication or warm-up varying
Splice placement varying from tyre to tyre

what_to_do.check: Split the tyres by building machine (green tyre barcode), press, cavity, mould and tester: following one building machine points to building, a press or mould to curing, one tester (check tyre too) to the tester
Check tester repeatability with the master tyre
Check splice placement and stagger

no_reading.has_happened: LFV was 0 or blank for some tyres; a real force variation cannot be 0.
can_happen_because: Test aborted: the bead did not seal or the tyre did not inflate
Tyre skipped, or a load cell or data-acquisition fault
Barcode join failed, so the result did not attach to the tyre

what_to_do.check: Check the tester alarm and status log, and the test pressure of the same tyres
Retest those tyres

off_target.has_happened: Many tyres have LFV above the limit; the LFV level has shifted up.
can_happen_because: Beads not parallel, or ply slipping unevenly at the bead (turn-up left and right)
Belt or tread placed off-centre; tread or sidewall uneven
Green tyre loaded off-centre in the mould
Tester: split rim misaligned, poor bead fit, rim runout, loadwheel alignment, or wrong rim width for the size
Warm-up time on the tester too short

what_to_do.check: Split the tyres by building machine (green tyre barcode), press, cavity, mould and tester: following one building machine points to building, a press or mould to curing, one tester (check tyre too) to the tester
Check the bead setter and the turn-up left and right
Check belt and tread centring
Run the master tyre; check rims with a dial indicator and the rim width in the recipe

spikes.has_happened: A few tyres have much higher LFV than the rest.
can_happen_because: Bead not seated, or a dry bead (lubrication missed)
Sidewall splice bulge
Green tyre crushed in storage

what_to_do.check: Retest the tyre
Inspect the sidewall and bead area
Check the bead lubrication station

jumping.has_happened: LFV swings above and below the control limits.
can_happen_because: Tyres from different building machines, presses or sizes mixed in one chart
Bead seating, lubrication or warm-up varying on the tester
Belt or tread placement varying from tyre to tyre

what_to_do.check: Split the tyres by building machine (green tyre barcode), press, cavity, mould and tester: following one building machine points to building, a press or mould to curing, one tester (check tyre too) to the tester
Check tester repeatability with the master tyre
Check belt and tread centring

Conicity.note: Sign conventions differ between testers, so check them before comparing testers.

no_reading.has_happened: Conicity was blank for some tyres. A single 0 can be real; many exact zeros in a row mean missing data.
can_happen_because: Test aborted, or only one direction was run
Data channel fault

what_to_do.check: Check the tester alarm log and whether both directions were run

off_target.has_happened: Conicity is consistently on one side.
can_happen_because: Belt placed off-centre against the tread and carcass (the most common cause)
Tread or belt forming a cone: one shoulder thicker than the other
Green tyre off-centre in the mould, top and bottom curing differently, or uneven post-cure cooling
A deliberate design bias in the spec
Tester: load cell zero, direction run, or spindle and loadwheel alignment (suspect this if conicity and ply steer shift together)

what_to_do.check: Check belt and tread centring, the guides and the transfer ring
Measure the tread profile gauge on the left and right shoulders
Split conicity by press and cavity; check platen temperatures
Confirm the spec target, then run the master tyre in both directions

spikes.has_happened: A few tyres have conicity far from the rest.
can_happen_because: A single misplaced belt or tread
Bead not seated during the test

what_to_do.check: Retest the tyre
Check the building record of those tyres (barcode)

jumping.has_happened: Conicity swings both ways.
can_happen_because: Belt or tread placement varying from tyre to tyre
Bead seating or lubrication varying
Warm-up on the tester too short
Rim misalignment
Testers with different sign conventions mixed in one chart

what_to_do.check: Do a repeatability study with the master tyre; if the tester's own spread is small, the scatter comes from the process
Split the chart by tester
Check belt and tread centring

Inflation Pressure.note: Test pressure is a tester and seal value, not a tyre result. Tyres tested outside the band have biased RFV, LFV and conicity: flag and retest them.

no_reading.has_happened: Test pressure was 0 or blank for some tyres.
can_happen_because: Bead never sealed, so the tyre did not inflate
Test aborted, air supply off, or a channel fault

what_to_do.check: Check the tester alarm log; RFV present with 0 pressure points to a data or transducer problem
Check bead lubrication and the rim seal

off_target.has_happened: Test pressure is consistently higher (or lower) than normal.
can_happen_because: Wrong pressure setpoint for the size
Pressure transducer offset, or low supply air
Fouled pressure regulator
Different sizes or testers with different setpoints mixed together

what_to_do.check: Compare the median pressure per tester and size
Calibrate the transducer against a reference gauge
Service the regulator and check the supply air

spikes.has_happened: A few tyres were tested at a much lower (or higher) pressure.
can_happen_because: Air leaking at the upper bead on heavy or soft-sidewall tyres
Dry bead (lubrication missed)
Rim width not matching the bead
Damaged bead or rim

what_to_do.check: Check the lubrication station and the rim seal face
Retest those tyres; their RFV, LFV and conicity are not reliable

jumping.has_happened: Test pressure swings up and down.
can_happen_because: Pressure-reducing valve unstable
Seal at the bead varying from tyre to tyre
Size or recipe changes inside the window

what_to_do.check: Look at the pressure trace per test; clean or replace the valve
Split the chart by size
